question.text: A fund manager explains to the Investment Committee: 'Enterprise Value reflects the operating value of the business regardless of capital structure, while Equity Value reflects the value of the shareholders' residual claim'. Which ONE of the following correctly expresses the EV-to-Equity-Value bridge?

answer.text: Equity Value = EV - EBITDA + Working Capital
Equity Value = EV x (1 - Debt/Equity ratio)
Equity Value = EV + Total Debt + Preference Capital - Cash
Equity Value = EV - Total Debt (net of cash) - Preference Capital

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 14.4.1, EV = Equity Value + Total Debt (net of cash) + Preference Capital, which rearranges to Equity Value = EV - Total Debt (net of cash) - Preference Capital. EV captures the whole capital pie; equity gets what's left after all senior claims. **The Trap:** Option A reverses the signs. Option C mixes operating with balance-sheet items. Option D is a nonsensical ratio manipulation. **Cross-Exam Context:** XV and XXI-B both test this bridge; XIX-C is specifically strict on the 'net of cash' qualifier and the preference-capital adjustment. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** In every IC valuation memo, display the EV-to-Equity bridge as a waterfall chart. It forces clarity on hidden liabilities (ESOP overhang, earnouts, indemnity escrows) that reduce effective equity value to shareholders.
